proof:
# Largest-parity-class mass cannot supply a positive-dimensional depth certificate

The proposed inequality

    max_y raw_depth(y) >= gamma_d max_r mu(S_r)       (X)

is false even for actual lattice products and every d>=1. Its failure
can be arbitrarily large as the integer dimension increases. This is
an obstruction to charging a whole largest parity class to one center,
not to OC or to the occupied-parity-count target gamma_d M/k(P).

Let n>=3. Put Q=2 Delta_n, where

    Delta_n={z in R^n:z_i>=0, sum_i z_i<=1}.

Let K be a d-dimensional simplex of volume V>0, and take the convex
body C=Q times K. The complete integer base set P consists exactly of

    0, 2e_i (1<=i<=n),
    e_i (1<=i<=n), e_i+e_j (1<=i<j<=n).

These are all nonnegative integer vectors with coordinate sum at most2.
Thus P is the set of n+1 vertices of Q and the midpoints of all of its
edges. Its size is N=(n+1)(n+2)/2. Every continuous fiber is exactly K.

The all-even parity class consists of the n+1 vertices and has mass
(n+1)V. Every other occupied parity class is a singleton edge midpoint,
since its parity vector has either one or two1's and uniquely identifies
that midpoint. In particular the largest parity-class mass is (n+1)V.

## Explicit full-plane cap covers of small mass

Write lambda_0(z)=1-(sum_i z_i)/2 and lambda_i(z)=z_i/2 for i>=1
for the affine barycentric coordinates on Q. For a base p in P let I
index its minimal simplex face: |I|=1 if p is a vertex, and |I|=2 if
p is an edge midpoint. Define

    ell_I(z)=sum_(j not in I) lambda_j(z).

On P this is nonnegative, is zero exactly at the points of that face,
and is at least1/2 at every other base. The face contains respectively
one or three bases of P.

Let L_0(x),...,L_d(x) be the affine barycentric coordinates of K, so
sum_r L_r(x)=1 for every x in R^d. The d+1 ordinary centroid vertex
caps L_r(x)>=1/(d+1) each have volume gamma_d V. This follows directly:
the cap at vertex r is the homothetic copy of K about that vertex
with scale d/(d+1).

For this face I use the ambient closed halfspaces

    H_(I,r)={ (z,x):L_r(x)-2 ell_I(z)>=1/(d+1) },
                                     r=0,...,d.     (1)

At every base of the face, they cover the ENTIRE continuous plane,
because the L_r sum to one and at least one is >=1/(d+1). At a base
outside the face, no point of its K-fiber belongs to any cap (1): on K,
L_r<=1, so the left side is at most1-2*(1/2)=0<1/(d+1).
Each of these is a genuine halfspace with a nonzero continuous normal.

Consequently its exact captured mixed mass is gamma_d V for a vertex
face and3 gamma_d V for an edge face. Using these finitely many covers
at all the bases proves

    max_y raw_depth(y) <=3 gamma_d V.                (2)

For n>=3 this is strictly smaller than gamma_d(n+1)V, disproving (X)
with a complete finite cap certificate. More strongly the ratio of
the left side of (X) to its proposed right side is at most3/(n+1),
which tends to zero. Thus no universal positive constant multiplying
the right side repairs this particular strongest-parity-class claim.

## Compatibility with OC

For n=3, the original target is gamma_d(10V)/8. At the point with base
e_1 and continuous coordinate the centroid g of K, retain just the
three fibers at0,e_1,2e_1. For any containing halfspace, move its
boundary through this point. According to the sign of its e_1 base
coefficient, either the fibers at0,e_1 or those at e_1,2e_1 have
continuous thresholds no greater than the through-g threshold. Each
therefore contributes at least gamma_d V by ordinary Grünbaum. If
the continuous normal is zero, the same two fibers are fully contained.
This gives raw depth at least2 gamma_d V, above10 gamma_d V/8.

For n>=4, N<=2^n. Equality of the fiber volumes therefore makes any
fiber heavy enough: its ordinary centroid alone contributes
gamma_d V>=gamma_d NV/2^n. The inequality N<=2^n holds at n=4
(15<=16) and propagates because N_(n+1)/N_n=(n+3)/(n+1)<2.

So the family has a separately proved OC point in every stated
dimension. The source is fully nondegenerate, has a product structure,
and includes every integer fiber. Its role is to prevent the new
same-coset mixed BM inequality from being promoted to a false
largest-parity-mass depth guarantee. Global midpoint-density collisions
and cap charging remain genuine issues.
